answer: A new participant locks 25 POA for twelve epochs and must finish five distinct jobs, each checked by three randomly assigned reviewers who share no funder. Two matching approvals pass; proven collusion burns 15% of the bond. Public signatures and transfer graphs make attacks visible: a knoll marks the minimum reputation needed for paid work, a spiral of repeated funding reveals cloned accounts, and a vine of identical reviewer sets exposes collusion rings. Because sybils must each post a bond and build their own verified trail, mass identity farming loses money.
